questions.question: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease is caused by duplication of the peripheral myelin protein-22 (PMP22) gene on which chromosome?
questions.solution:
Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease, specifically type 1A, is caused by the duplication of the PMP22 gene located on Chromosome 17.
  • The PMP22 protein is a critical component of myelin, the protective sheath that insulates peripheral nerves.
  • Extra copies of this gene lead to an overproduction of the protein, causing the myelin sheath to become unstable and disintegrate over time.
  • Symptoms: This results in muscle weakness, atrophy, and loss of sensation in the feet, legs, hands, and arms.

questions.question: Who mentioned ecosystem as 'the basic unit in ecology' in 1956?
questions.solution:
Francis Evans is the ecologist who described the ecosystem as the 'basic unit in ecology' in his 1956 paper.
  • While A.G. Tansley originally coined the term 'ecosystem' in 1935, Evans emphasized its role as the fundamental functional unit for studying the interactions between biotic and abiotic components.
  • Context: This concept shifted the focus of ecology from merely identifying species to understanding the flow of energy and cycling of matter.

questions.question: In which year did Walter Fleming stain the chromosomes to see them clearly and describe the entire process of mitosis?
questions.solution:
In 1882, the German biologist Walther Flemming published his seminal work, Zellsubstanz, Kern und Zelltheilung, where he described the process of mitosis.
  • Flemming used aniline dyes to stain the thread-like structures in the nucleus, which he called 'chromatin' (later known as chromosomes).
  • He was the first to observe and describe the longitudinal splitting of chromosomes during cell division.
  • Fact: The term 'mitosis' comes from the Greek word 'mitos,' meaning 'thread,' referring to the appearance of the chromosomes.

questions.question: In which year was the fluid mosaic model proposed by Singer and Nicolson? The model commonly represented cell membrane structure and dynamics.
questions.solution:
The Fluid Mosaic Model was proposed by S.J. Singer and G.L. Nicolson in 1972.
  • This model describes the cell membrane as a tapestry of molecules (phospholipids, cholesterols, and proteins) that are constantly moving.
  • The 'fluid' part refers to the lateral movement of lipids and proteins, while 'mosaic' refers to the diverse pattern of proteins embedded in or attached to the lipid bilayer.
  • Significance: It remains the most widely accepted model for explaining the structure and function of biological membranes.

questions.question: Which amino acid is a precursor to serotonin, a neurotransmitter that regulates your appetite, sleep and mood?
questions.solution:
Tryptophan is the essential amino acid that serves as the primary precursor to serotonin.
  • In the body, tryptophan is converted into 5-hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP) and then into serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine).
  • Serotonin is a vital neurotransmitter often called the 'feel-good' hormone because of its role in stabilizing mood and regulating sleep cycles (as a precursor to melatonin).
  • Dietary Source: Since the human body cannot synthesize tryptophan, it must be obtained from protein-rich foods like turkey, eggs, and cheese.
